source_text: πρὶν ὅλως τοὺς περὶ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς ὀφθῆναι τύπους, καὶ τὰ ἐπ' αὐτῆς γενέσθαι προστάγματα, τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ χρυσῇ στάμνῳ κατεχρησμῴδησε λόγον, εἰδὼς τὸ ἐσόμενον. Μετὰ δέ γε τὴν πῆξιν τῆς ὅλης σκηνῆς ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς εὑρήσομεν τὴν ῥάβδον τὴν Ἀαρὼν εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰσκεκομισμένην. Ἐν δὲ τῷ Λευϊτικῷ προσεπενομοθέτει Θεὸς περί τε λυχνίας, καὶ μὴν καὶ τραπέζης τῆς ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ. Νομομαθὴς δὲ ὑπάρχων ὁ σοφώτατος Παῦλος, παρίησι μὲν ὅλως τῶν γεγονότων οὐδὲν, διαμέμνηται δὲ πρώτων τε καὶ μέσων καὶ τελευταίων. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. Φράζε δὴ οὖν ἕκαστα σαφῶς καὶ διεσταλμένως· βαθὺς γάρ που πάντως ὁ ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἐστι λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Ναὶ, λέγεις ὀρθῶς. Ἔχει γὰρ ὧδε τὸ χρῆμα κατὰ ἀλήθειαν. Ποιήσομαι δὲ τῶν διηγημάτων καὶ τὴν στάμνον ἀρχήν. Ὑετοῦ μὲν γοῦν δίκην καθίει Θεὸς τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ τὸ μάννα κατὰ τὴν ἔρημον· τροφὴ γὰρ τοῦτο καὶ ἄρτος αὐτοῖς ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ. Ἀλλ' ὅτι μὴ μέχρι τῶν αἰσθητῶν τὸ δρώμενον ἦν· ἀναφέρει γάρ τε ὥσπερ διὰ τύπου καὶ σκιᾶς ἐπὶ τὸ χρῆναι νοεῖν, ὅτι παρέσται κατὰ καιροὺς ὁ ἄνωθεν ἡμῖν καὶ ἐκ Πατρὸς Λόγος, ὡς ἄρτος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ὡς καὶ ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν Δαβὶδ ὑποφαίνει λέγων· «Ἄρτον οὐρανοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς, ἄρτον ἀγγέλων ἔφαγεν ἄνθρωπος.» Καὶ οὔτι πού φαμεν τὸ μάννα τὸ αἰσθητὸν ἄρτον εἶναι τὸν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀγγέλων. Τρέφεται μὲν γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα πνευματικῶς, σῶμα δὲ αὖ κατ' ἰδίαν φύσιν, τοῦτ' ἔστι, σωματικῶς. Τροφὴ δὲ ἀγγέλων καὶ ἄρτος ὁ πρέπων οὐρανοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἄνω πνεύμασιν, ὁ ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγος. Τὸ μάννα δὴ οὖν ἐδήλου Χριστόν. Οὐδὲν δὲ ὁ τύπος τὸ ὠφελοῦν ἔχει, μὴ τῆς ἀληθείας εἰσδεδεγμένης. Σκιὰ γὰρ τοῦτο ἐκείνης, οὐ δι' ἑαυτὸ κυρίως γεγονὸς, ἀλλ' ἵνα τι τῶν ἀμεινόνων ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ ζωγραφῇ. Διὰ τοῦτο Χριστὸς τοῖς Ἰουδαίων δήμοις σοφὴν ἐποιεῖτο τὴν ἐπίπληξιν, ὅτι μὴ μᾶλλον αὐτὸν ὡς ἀλήθειαν, ἀλλὰ Μωσέα θαυμάζουσι, τῶν τύπων τὸν ὑπουργόν. Ἔφη γὰρ οὕτως, «Ἀμὴν, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, Μωσῆς ὑμῖν δέδωκε τὸ μάννα· ὁ γὰρ ἄρτος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβὰς, καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ. Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν.» Εἰκόνα δὴ οὖν τὸ μάννα τιθεὶς τοῦ ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταφοιτήσαντος Λόγου, τὰ ἐπί γε τῇ στάμνῳ κεχρησμῴδηκε Θεός. Γέγραπται δὲ οὕτως· «Εἶπε δὲ Μωσῆς· Τοῦτο τὸ ῥῆμα, ὃ συνέταξε Κύριος, Πλήσατε τὸ γομὸρ τοῦ μάννα, εἰς ἀποθήκην εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν, ἵνα ἴδωσι τὸν ἄρτον, ὃν ἐφάγετε ὑμεῖς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ὡς ἐξήγαγεν ὑμᾶς Κύριος ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου. Καὶ εἶπε Μωσῆς πρὸς Ἀαρών· Λάβε στάμνον χρυσοῦν ἕνα, καὶ ἔμβαλε εἰς αὐτὸν πλῆρες τὸ γομὸρ τοῦ μάννα, καὶ ἀποθήσεις αὐτὸ ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰς διατήρησιν εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν, ὃν τρόπον συνέταξε Κύριος τῷ Μωσῇ. Καὶ ἀπέθετο Ἀαρὼν ἔναντι τοῦ μαρτυρίου, εἰς διατήρησιν.» Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐλέγομεν ὅτι τὸν θεῖον ἔχουσα λόγον ἡ κιβωτὸς ὑπεδήλου τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ· Θεοῦ γὰρ ἦν Λόγος ὡς ἐν
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. of Cyril] before at all the types (τύπος) about the holy tent (σκηνή) were seen (ὁράω, aor. pass. inf.) and the commands (πρόσταγμα) about it came to be, he uttered-as-oracle (καταχρησμῳδέω) the word about the golden jar (στάμνος χρυσῆ), knowing what would be (τὸ ἐσόμενον). After the fixing (πῆξις) of the whole tent, in Numbers we will find the rod (ῥάβδος) of Aaron brought into (εἰσκομίζω, pf. pass.) the Holy of Holies. In Leviticus God further legislated (προσεπινομοθετέω) about lampstand (λυχνία) and table (τράπεζα) in the first tent. Paul, most wise, being law-learned (νομομαθής), passes over (παρίημι) nothing at all of what happened, but recalls (διαμέμνημαι) first, middle and last things. — PALL.: Best said (ἄριστα). Tell (φράζω) each clearly and distinctly (διεσταλμένως); for deep (βαθύς) surely is the account (λόγος) about them. — CYR.: Yes, you say rightly; the thing holds so according to truth (κατὰ ἀλήθειαν). I will make the jar the beginning (ἀρχή) of my narrations (διήγημα). Like rain (ὑετοῦ δίκην) God sent down (καθίημι) the manna to those of Israel in the desert (ἔρημος); for this was food (τροφή) and bread (ἄρτος) to them from above and from heaven. But what was done (τὸ δρώμενον) was not as far as sensibles (τὰ αἰσθητά) only; it carries up (ἀναφέρω) as through type and shadow (σκιά) to the need to understand (νοεῖν) that the Word (Λόγος) from above and from the Father will be present (πάρειμι) to us in due seasons (κατὰ καιρούς), as bread from heaven, as divine David indicates (ὑποφαίνω), saying: bread of heaven he gave them, bread of angels man ate [LXX Ps 77:24–25]. And we by no means say the sensible manna is the bread from heaven and of angels. For spirit (πνεῦμα) is nourished (τρέφω) spiritually (πνευματικῶς), body by its own nature (φύσις), i.e. bodily (σωματικῶς). Food of angels and bread befitting (πρέπων) the heavens and the spirits above is the Word from God the Father. So the manna showed (δηλόω) Christ. The type has nothing profiting (τὸ ὠφελοῦν) if the truth (ἀλήθεια) is not received (εἰσδέχομαι). For it is a shadow of that, not come about properly (κυρίως) for its own sake, but so that it may paint (ζωγραφέω) in itself something of the better things (τὰ ἀμείνονα). Therefore Christ made a wise rebuke (ἐπίπληξις) to the crowds (δῆμοι) of the Jews, that they wonder at (θαυμάζω) not him rather as truth but Moses, the minister (ὑπουργός) of the types. He said: Amen amen I say to you, Moses has given you the manna; for (γάρ) the bread of God is the one who came down (καταβάς) from heaven and gives life (ζωή) to the world; I am the living bread. Setting (τίθημι) the manna, then, as an image (εἰκών) of the Word who came down (καταφοιτάω) from above and from heaven, God has oracled the things about the jar. It is written: Moses said: This is the word which the Lord commanded (συντάσσω): Fill the gomor (γομόρ = omer) of manna for storage (ἀποθήκη) for your generations (γενεαί), that they may see the bread you ate in the desert, as the Lord led you out of the land of Egypt. Moses said to Aaron: Take one golden jar, put in it full the gomor of manna, and you will lay it up (ἀποτίθημι) before God for keeping (διατήρησις) for your generations, as the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron laid it up before the testimony (μαρτύριον) for keeping [Exod 16:32–34]. For as we were saying that the ark (κιβωτός), having the divine word (θεῖος λόγος), indicated (ὑποδηλόω) Emmanuel; for it was God's Word (Λόγος) as in [a holy temple…, continues §12].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …before the patterns of the holy tent had been shown at all, and the commands about it given, God uttered the oracle about the golden jar (Exodus 16:32–34), since he knew what was to come. After the whole tent had been set up, we shall find in Numbers that Aaron’s rod was brought into the Holy of Holies (Numbers 17:10). And in Leviticus God gave further laws about the lampstand and the table in the first tent (Leviticus 24:1–9). And Paul, most wise and learned in the law, leaves out nothing at all of what took place, but recalls the first things, the middle ones and the last.
Palladius: Very well said. Then explain each thing clearly and point by point; for surely there is a deep meaning in them.

Cyril: Yes, you are right; for that is how the matter truly stands. I will make the jar the starting point of my account. God sent the manna down like rain on the people of Israel in the wilderness; for this was their food and bread from above, from heaven (Exodus 16:4). But what was done did not stop at things of sense. As through a type and a shadow, it leads us up to understand that in due time the Word would come to us from above and from the Father, as bread from heaven, just as the divine David hints to us when he says: ‘He gave them the bread of heaven; man ate the bread of angels’ (Psalm 78:24–25). We certainly do not say that the physical manna was the bread from heaven and of angels. For a spirit is fed spiritually, and a body according to its own nature, that is, bodily. The food of angels, the bread fit for the heavens and for the spirits above, is the Word who is from God the Father. So the manna signified Christ. Yet the type is of no use unless the truth has been received. For it is a shadow of the truth, not made chiefly for its own sake, but so that it might paint in itself a picture of something better. That is why Christ gave the crowds of the Jews a wise rebuke, because they admired, not him as the truth, but Moses, the servant of the types. For he said: ‘Truly, truly, I say to you, Moses has given you the manna; but the bread of God is he who came down from heaven and gives life to the world. I am the living bread’ (John 6:32–33, 51). So it was in making the manna an image of the Word who came down from above, from heaven, that God gave the oracle about the jar. It is written thus: ‘And Moses said: This is the word which the Lord commanded: Fill the omer with manna, to be laid up for your generations, so that they may see the bread which you ate in the wilderness, when the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt. And Moses said to Aaron: Take one golden jar, and put into it a full omer of manna, and lay it up before God, to be kept for your generations, as the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron laid it up before the testimony, to be kept’ (Exodus 16:32–34). anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence, continuing §10 (‘For in Exodus, even…’); the subject of κατεχρησμῴδησε is God (named in §10’s frame), supplied in English. Psalm 78:24–25 is LXX Psalm 77:24–25 (English numbering given). Exodus 16:33: the LXX adds ‘golden’ (στάμνον χρυσοῦν) where the Hebrew has only ‘a jar’; Cyril follows the LXX; γομόρ rendered ‘omer’. John 6:32–33, 51: the printed text is a free paraphrase and lacks the ‘not’ of John 6:32 (οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν); translated as printed, without restoring the negation; its γάρ is rendered ‘but’ because the clause contrasts the manna with the bread of God. ‘The living bread’ matches John 6:51 (ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν), not 6:35. ‘The divine word’ (θεῖον λόγον) held by the ark means the tablets of the law; lower case to keep it apart from the Word (Λόγος) in the next clause, where Cyril plays on the two. ‘Numbers’ refers to Numbers 17:10 (LXX 17:25), where Aaron’s rod is laid up before the testimony; Cyril’s ‘Holy of Holies’ is his reading, following Hebrews 9:4. ‘Leviticus’ = Leviticus 24:1–9 (lamp oil, twelve loaves), quoted in §14. Paul’s summary of the tent (Hebrews 9:1–5) was quoted in §10 and is not cited again here. Reviewer: ‘like rain … bread from above, from heaven’ alludes to Exodus 16:4 (LXX ὕω ὑμῖν ἄρτους ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ), now cited inline. τὸ μάννα τὸ αἰσθητόν rendered ‘the physical manna’ (here and in §12) instead of ‘the manna of sense’.
